from.name: Sven Hermans
from.org: Bouwmarkt Noord, a DIY chain with 18 stores

subject: Time management course for store managers?
mail: Hi, my store managers are always behind on their admin, and staff schedules keep getting published late. I think they need a time management course. Could you find a good provider? Bonus points if it fits in one afternoon.
snippets: 18 stores, each with one store manager.
Company policy: staff schedules are published 7 days in advance.
Head office survey: store managers say they 'feel overloaded'.

hidden_facts.fact: Schedules started going out late in June, when a new scheduling tool went live. Building a week's schedule now takes about three hours instead of 45 minutes.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks since when, or what changed recently.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Since when? Summer, I'd say. June. Ah. That's when we got the new planning tool. It's very powerful. It takes three hours to make one schedule.

hidden_facts.fact: Only 5 of the 18 managers publish late, and all 5 run stores with more than 40 staff.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks who exactly is late, or whether it's all managers.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Not all of them, no. Five. The big stores, now that I look at the list. Over forty people each.

best_question: Since when have schedules been late, and what changed around that time?
weak_patterns: Asking how long the course should be, or online versus classroom.
Asking which time management method they prefer.
Asking for the budget before understanding the problem.
debrief: 'Always behind' usually started somewhere. A strong intake asks since when and who exactly, which here points at a scheduling tool that triples the work in the five biggest stores. Fix or train on the tool; nobody needs a time management course.
